facts.text: Dixon Springs earned its name from Revolutionary War veteran Tilman Dixon, one of the first settlers in Middle Tennessee around 1787.
Dixona, the 1787 log home of Tilman Dixon, hosted Smith County's first court session in 1799 and welcomed future French king Louis Philippe in 1797.
Dixona, one of Middle Tennessee's oldest structures, is on the National Register of Historic Places and remains a private residence on a 148‑acre farm with a spring.
A Civil War skirmish on June 20, 1863, saw Confederate soldiers clash with Union troops guarding a plantation trench near Dixon Springs.
By the late 19th century, Dixon Springs had grown into a modest town center with general stores, mills, hotels, an academy, and a union church supporting local farming.
Located in northern Smith County, Dixon Springs lies about 58 miles northeast of Nashville and sits near tributaries of the Cumberland River that historically helped transport crops.
